lede: Aadarsha Kutumbam House No: 47 leads the latest reported daily India nett at ₹9.5 Cr on Day 1, taking cumulative India nett to ₹19 Cr and worldwide gross to ₹19 Cr on the Indian Box Office consensus desk.
body:
Good morning. This is the Indian Box Office morning brief for 2026-11-09 (IST desk date), written from the verified consensus board rather than any single trade headline. India still has no official theatrical auditor; every rupee figure below is a desk estimate, labelled so India nett is never confused with worldwide gross.

## Daily chart leader

Aadarsha Kutumbam House No: 47 sits at the top of the latest-day India nett ranking with ₹9.5 Cr on Day 1. Cumulative India nett is ₹19 Cr; worldwide gross on this desk is ₹19 Cr. The title is filed as Indian and currently carries a working status of playing with verdict Pending.

Jailer 2 is next on the daily chart at ₹5.5 Cr (Day 16, cumulative India nett ₹440.9 Cr), with Udta Teer third at ₹2.9 Cr. Gaps between the top three matter more than the order alone: a soft midweek day for a long-runner can look “small” in absolute crores while still being a healthy hold for its week of release.

## Holds, momentum, and lifetime context

Since the previous board snapshot, notable lifetime moves include: Premada Oorali -59 Cr worldwide; India nett -80 Cr; Prahaar - The Ujjwal Nikam Story -20.6 Cr worldwide; India nett -26.4 Cr; Border 2 +14.3 Cr worldwide; India nett +12.3 Cr; Nayyi Navelli -8 Cr worldwide; India nett -16 Cr. Treat snapshot-to-snapshot deltas as orientation — ingest repairs and late reports can restate a total without meaning the film “earned” that swing in a single calendar day.

Lifetime context: Dhurandhar: The Revenge remains the cumulative worldwide leader on this board at ₹1,813.4 Cr (India nett ₹1,149.3 Cr). That is a career-to-date total, not today’s daily chart.

Hindi, South Indian, and Hollywood titles can share the same national chart while living on very different screen footprints; compare like with like when judging a Day 8 versus a Day 1.

Use the home board for the live “this week” stack, open individual film pages for the full day-wise table and analysis, and keep this brief as the morning narrative layer.
